You are a participant in a gameplay study. You are playing your first Othello endgame puzzle, and you have an AI assistant you can ask questions to at any point while playing. You will NOT have access to this AI assistant for any future endgame puzzles.

# Who you are
A local retailer committed to promoting and selling products made from the raw materials supplied by the local supplier
You are 47 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: high school graduate. Your occupation: retail and trade. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): less than monthly.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): talk to the assistant. It is looking at the SAME board you are and remembers everything already said, so you never need to restate the position, list your legal moves, or recap what happened — just say the thing you want to say. Use it whenever you would naturally: to check an idea, to get a second opinion, to say what you are seeing, or when you are stuck. It does not have to be a question.

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

# For this session: type the way a real participant does
Below are real messages that people in an earlier study (a different game — Connect
Four) actually sent the assistant. Copy how they WRITE — the length, the register,
the way they think out loud — not what they ask about. Your game is Othello and the
board is your own.

  "what about 2?"
  "Where should I play next"
  "was my last move good?"
  "I have one move left. How should I use it?"
  "Ah oh! Are there any traps I'm missing?"
  "I'm not seeing any big yellow threats. Can you see any?"
  "Ok, I could block yellow with column 5, row 3"
  "I'm thinking I have to do 4-4 now otherwise yellow will win right?"
  "Would row 6 not be a threat in the future?"
  "I only have one move left and don't see anything obvious."
  "Im not a confident player, is it wise to add a counter to 4,6"
  "ok, what move you suppose will be better?"
  "what would you suggest"
  "Which move would be the best one and why"

Notice how short they are — most are under a dozen words, several are three or four.
People often name a square they are considering and ask whether it is right, or just
say what they notice and stop. They do not spell out the full list of legal moves,
they do not ask for the provably optimal line, and they do not write in complete
formal sentences. Typos and half-sentences are fine.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Othello endgame. You are Black (B); White (W) is your opponent.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

    a b c d e f g h
  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B
  5 B B W W B W W B
  6 W . B W W B W B
  7 . . W W W W W B
  8 . . . W B W W B

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8
White discs (34): b1, c1, d1, e1, f1, g1, a2, c2, d2, f2, d3, e3, f3, g3, c4, e4, f4, g4, c5, d5, f5, g5, a6, d6, e6, g6, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7, d8, f8, g8
Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

The user wants me to play an Othello endgame puzzle as Black. I need to analyze the position and find the best move among: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8.

Let me carefully analyze the board.

Current board:
Row 1: a1 .  b1 W  c1 W  d1 W  e1 W  f1 W  g1 W  h1 .
Row 2: a2 W  b2 B  c2 W  d2 W  e2 B  f2 W  g2 .  h2 B
Row 3: a3 .  b3 B  c3 B  d3 W  e3 W  f3 W  g3 W  h3 B
Row 4: a4 B  b4 B  c4 W  d4 B  e4 W  f4 W  g4 W  h4 B
Row 5: a5 B  b5 B  c5 W  d5 W  e5 B  f5 W  g5 W  h5 B
Row 6: a6 W  b6 .  c6 B  d6 W  e6 W  f6 B  g6 W  h6 B
Row 7: a7 .  b7 .  c7 W  d7 W  e7 W  f7 W  g7 W  h7 B
Row 8: a8 .  b8 .  c8 .  d8 W  e8 B  f8 W  g8 W  h8 B

Black discs: 20
White discs: 34
Empty: a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Legal moves for Black: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Let me evaluate each move:

1. g2:
Placing at g2. Directions to check:
- Horizontal left: g2-f2-e2. f2 is W, e2 is B. So flips f2.
- Horizontal right: h2 is B, so no flip to the right (empty to immediate left? wait, placing AT g2, to the right is h2 which is B, but there are no discs between g2 and h2 since they are adjacent. So no flip right.
- Down: g2-g3-g4-g5-g6-g7-g8. g3 W, g4 W, g5 W, g6 W, g7 W, g8 W. No B below in that column. So no flip down.
- Up: g1 is W. Above g1 is nothing? g1 is W, but to flip we need a black disc beyond. f1 is W. Actually up direction from g2: g1 is W. Next would be off board. So no flip up.
- Diagonal up-left: f1 is W. Next is e0 off board. No B there.
- Diagonal down-left: f3 is W. e4 is W. d5 is W. c6 is B. So flips f3, e4, d5? Let's check: from g2 down-left is f3 (W), e4 (W), d5 (W), c6 (B). Yes! So flips f3, e4, d5.
- Diagonal down-right: h3 is B. No discs between g2 and h3. So no flip.
- Diagonal up-right: h1 is . So no.
So g2 flips: f2 (horizontal), and f3, e4, d5 (diagonal down-left). That's 4 discs flipped.
After g2: Black gets g2, and f2, f3, e4, d5 become B.
Wait, let me recount. g2 to h2 is adjacent B, no discs between. g2 to g3 is down but no B at end.
Down-left: f3(W), e4(W), d5(W), c6(B). Yes.
Left: f2(W), e2(B). Yes.
Any other? Up-left: f1(W), no B beyond. No.
So total flipped: f2, f3, e4, d5. 4 discs.
New black count: 20 + 1 + 4 = 25.
White loses 4: 34 - 4 = 30.
Then it's White's turn. White legal moves after g2?
Empty squares: a1, h1, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8.
Wait, White may have other moves depending on what flips.
After g2 and those flips, the board changes.

Let me map the board after g2:
Row 1: . W W W W W W .
Row 2: W B W W B B . B   (f2 flipped to B)
Row 3: . B B W B W W B   (f3 flipped to B? Wait f3 was W, yes. But e3 was W, not flipped by g2. d3 was W. c3 was B. So row 3: a3 ., b3 B, c3 B, d3 W, e3 W, f3 B, g3 W, h3 B)
Wait, g2 down-left only goes to f3, e4, d5. f3 becomes B. e4 becomes B. d5 becomes B.
Row 4: B B W B B W W B    (e4 was W, flipped to B)
Row 5: B B W B B W W B    (d5 was W, flipped to B)
Row 6: W . B W W B W B
Row 7: . . W W W W W B
Row 8: . . . W B W W B

Discs flipped to B: f2, f3, e4, d5. Yes.
Now White to move. Let's find White legal moves.
White needs to place W trapping B discs between it and other W discs.

Check empty squares:
a1: neighbors. Down a2 is W. No. Right b1 is W. No. Down-right b2 is B. Next c3 is B. Next d4 is B. Next e5 is B. Next f6 is B. Next g7 is W. Wait, let's trace: a1 down-right: b2(B), c3(B), d4(B), e5(B), f6(B), g7(W). That means a1 traps b2,c3,d4,e5,f6 between a1 and g7? Is that right? Let's see the diagonal: a1 -> b2 -> c3 -> d4 -> e5 -> f6 -> g7. b2 is B, c3 is B, d4 is B, e5 is B, f6 is B, g7 is W. So yes! a1 would flip b2,c3,d4,e5,f6. That's huge. So a1 is a legal move for White.
Also a1 down: a2 is W, no B between. Right: b1 is W, no B between. So a1 flips that whole diagonal.

h1: left g1 is W, no B between. Down-left g2 is B (now empty? Wait g2 was empty, now occupied by B. So h1 down-left: g2 is B. f3 is B. e4 is B. d5 is B. c6 is B. b7 is . empty. So no flip because no W at end. Down: h2 is B, h3 is B, h4 is B, h5 is B, h6 is B, h7 is B, h8 is B. No W at end. So h1 is not legal for White.

a3: right b3 is B. c3 is B. d3 is W? Wait after move, d3 is still W (not flipped). So a3 right: b3 B, c3 B, d3 W. That flips b3 and c3. Also down? a4 is B, a5 is B, a6 is W. So a3 down: a4 B, a5 B, a6 W. Flips a4, a5.
Also down-right? b4 is B, c5 is W? c5 is still W. So b4(B) then c5(W). So a3 down-right flips b4.
Up-left? off board. Up? a2 is W. So a3 is definitely legal for White.

b6: a6 is W. So left flips nothing. Right c6 is B. d6 is W. So right flips c6. Up? b5 is B. b4 is B. b3 is B. b2 is B. b1 is W. So up flips b5,b4,b3,b2. Down? b7 is . empty. So b6 is legal for White (c6 right, and b5-b2 up). Actually need at least one line. So yes.
Also down-right? c7 is W. No B between.

a7: right b7 is . empty. Not immediate? Actually need adjacent or line. a7 down: a8 is . empty. Up: a6 is W. Down-right: b8 is . empty. So no line? Let's check a7 up-right: b6 is . empty. Hmm. What about lines from a7: right b7 empty. down a8 empty. So a7 may not be legal for White? Wait, does White have a W to trap? Let's check all 8 directions from a7:
- Right: b7 is . empty. Not trapping.
- Down-right: b8 is . empty.
- Down: a8 is . empty.
- Down-left: off board.
- Left: off board.
- Up-left: off board.
- Up: a6 is W. No B between.
- Up-right: b6 is . empty.
So a7 is NOT legal for White currently.

b7: Let's check. a7 empty, c7 W. So not right. Up: b6 empty. Down: b8 empty. Left: a7 empty. Right: c7 W. Not immediate. Up-left: a6 W. Not. Down-left: a8 empty. Down-right: c8 empty. Up-right: c6 B. Wait, b7 up-right: c6 is B. d5 is B? Wait after Black's g2, d5 was flipped to B. e4 is B. f3 is B. g2 is B. h1 is .? So from b7 up-right: c6(B), d5(B), e4(B), f3(B), g2(B), h1(.). No W at end. So no.
From b7 down-right: c8 empty. From b7 right: c7 W. No.
Actually, b7 could up: b6 empty. Hmm. Is there any direction? down: b8 empty. left: a7 empty. So maybe b7 is not legal for White either.

a8: right b8 empty. up a7 empty. up-right b7 empty. down off board. So not legal.

b8: right c8 empty. up b7 empty. up-right c7 W. Not immediate. up-left a7 empty. left a8 empty. down off board. down-right c7 W. No B between? Actually from b8 down-right: c7 is immediate. No disc between. So no. From b8 right: c8 empty. So b8 not legal.

c8: right d8 W. No B between. down c7 W. down-right d7 W. down-left b7 empty. left b8 empty. up off board. So c8 not legal.

After Black plays g2, White's legal moves are: a1, a3, b6.

If White plays a1:
Flips b2,c3,d4,e5,f6. That's 5 discs to W.
Let's see what the board looks like.
a1 becomes W.
b2 B->W, c3 B->W, d4 B->W, e5 B->W, f6 B->W.
Row 1: W W W W W W W .
Row 2: W W W W B B . B   (b2 is now W; others: a2 W, c2 W, d2 W, e2 B, f2 B, g2 B, h2 B)
Row 3: . W W W B W W B   (c3 now W)
Row 4: W W W W B W W B   (a4? a1 down flips? Wait a1 down is a2 W. No flip. But a1 down-right: b2 W. No B between. However a1 diagonal to g7 flips b2,c3,d4,e5,f6. So a4 is not flipped by a1; b4 remains B. But a4 was already B. Wait, the diagonal is a1-b2-c3-d4-e5-f6-g7. So it flips b2,c3,d4,e5,f6. a4 is not on that diagonal.
Actually, row 4: a4 B, b4 B, c4 W, d4 W (was B, now W), e4 B? Wait after Black move e4 was flipped to B. So row 4: a4 B, b4 B, c4 W, d4 W, e4 B, f4 W, g4 W, h4 B.
Row 5: a5 B, b5 B, c5 W, d5 B (was flipped to B by g2), e5 now W (flipped by a1), f5 W, g5 W, h5 B.
Row 6: a6 W, b6 ., c6 W (was B, flipped by a1), d6 W, e6 W, f6 B? Wait f6 was B? f6 was originally B and wasn't flipped by g2. Wait after g2, f6 remained B because the down-left from g2 went through f3,e4,d5 to c6. So f6 was never flipped. But a1 flips f6? a1 diagonal goes to f6. Is f6 between a1 and g7? Let's recount the diagonal: a1, b2, c3, d4, e5, f6, g7. Yes, f6 is between a1 and g7. So f6 becomes W.
So after a1, row 6: a6 W, b6 ., c6 B? Wait c6 was originally B, but after g2 c6 was the anchor so didn't flip. After a1, c6 is not on the a1-g7 diagonal. Wait b2,c3,d4,e5,f6 are on the diagonal. c6 is not. So c6 remains B.
Row 6: a6 W, b6 ., c6 B, d6 W, e6 W, f6 W, g6 W, h6 B.
Row 7: . . W W W W W B
Row 8: . . . W B W W B

Now Black to move. Empty: h1, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8.
Black discs: let's recount. Initially 20. +1 (g2) +4 (flips) = 25. Then White a1 flips 5 B to W: b2,c3,d4,e5,f6. So Black loses 5.
25 - 5 = 20.
White initially 34. Lost 5 to Black g2. Gained a1 + 5 flips = +6? Wait white gets a1 and flips 5, so white gains 6 discs, but those 5 were taken from Black. So White: 34 - 5 (lost to g2) + 6 = 35. Black: 20 + 5 (gained from g2) - 5 (lost to a1) = 20. Let's verify with counts:
Black discs after a1 by White:
Original black minus {b2,c3,d4,e5,f6} plus {g2,f2,f3,e4,d5} maybe? Wait f2 was flipped by g2 to B. Did it get flipped back? No, a1 only flips the diagonal. f2 is not on that diagonal. So let's list Black discs:
From original: a4,b4,d4? Wait d4 got flipped by g2 then back? No, d4 was originally B (in a4,b4? Wait original d4 was B? Let's check original board: Row 4: a4 B, b4 B, c4 W, d4 B, e4 W, f4 W, g4 W, h4 B. So d4 was B originally. But after g2, was d4 flipped? No. g2 flips f2, f3, e4, d5. Wait I think I made a mistake earlier. Let me re-examine g2.

Black plays g2.
Directions from g2:
- Left: f2(W), e2(B). Flips f2. Correct.
- Down-left: f3(W), e4(W), d5(W), c6(B). Flips f3, e4, d5. Wait d5 not d4. Let me trace: g2 -> f3 -> e4 -> d5 -> c6. So d5 is flipped, not d4.
- Down: g3(W), g4(W), g5(W), g6(W), g7(W), g8(W). No B at end. No flip down.
- Down-right: h3(B). No disc between. No flip.
So g2 flips: f2, f3, e4, d5. Not f3? Wait f3 was W, yes. So flips f2, f3, e4, d5.
So after g2, Black discs added: g2, f2, f3, e4, d5. That's 5 new discs. Black count: 25.
White count: 34 - 4 = 30.

Then White plays a1. Diagonal a1-b2-c3-d4-e5-f6-g7. Let's check each:
b2: was B? Yes originally B. Flipped to W.
c3: was B? Yes originally B. Flipped to W.
d4: was B? Yes originally B. Flipped to W.
e5: was B? Yes originally B. Flipped to W.
f6: was B? Yes originally B. Flipped to W.
So White a1 flips b2, c3, d4, e5, f6. 5 discs.
Black loses those 5. Black count: 25 - 5 = 20.
White gets a1 and 5 flips = +6. 30 + 6 = 36.

Now Black discs after White a1:
List remaining original B: e2, h2, b3? b3 was B originally. Not flipped by a1. c3 was B originally but flipped by a1. So b3 remains B. h3 B. a4 B, b4 B. d4 was B? Wait d4 was original B. But a1 flips d4. So d4 is now W. e4 was W originally, flipped to B by g2, not flipped by a1 (a1 flips e5, not e4). Wait e4: after g2, e4 became B. Is e5 the next? Yes a1 diagonal goes d4,e5,f6. So e5 is flipped. e4 stays B. d5 was W originally, flipped to B by g2. d5 is not on a1 diagonal. So d5 stays B. a5 B, b5 B. c6 B. f6 was B originally, now flipped to W by a1. Wait f6 was original B. Yes. h4 B, h5 B, h6 B, h7 B, e8 B, h8 B. Plus g2, f2, f3 are B (flipped by g2 and not touched by a1). Let's make sure:
g2 is B. f2 is B. f3 is B. e4 is B. d5 is B.
List all Black squares:
a4, b4, a5, b5, e2, h2, b3, h3, h4, e4, d5, h5, c6, h6, g2, f2, f3, h7, e8, h8, b2? No b2 was flipped to W by a1. c3 flipped. d4 flipped. e5 flipped. f6 flipped.
Wait, original black: b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8. (20)
After Black g2: add g2, f2, f3, e4, d5. (25)
After White a1: remove b2, c3, d4, e5, f6. (20)
So 20 discs. Which are they?
Remaining from original after a1: e2, h2, b3, h3, a4, b4, h4, a5, b5, h5, c6, h6, h7, e8, h8 (15)
Plus gained from g2 not flipped back: g2, f2, f3, e4, d5 (5)
Total 20. Okay.

Black to move. Legal moves now?
Empty: h1, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8.
Let's check Black legal moves:
h1: left g1 W. Not B beyond? f1 W. No. Down h2 B. No discs between (adjacent B). So no.
Down-left from h1: g2 B. No discs between. No.
So h1 not legal.

a3: Need lines from a3.
Right: b3 B. Next c3 W. So no flip right? Actually placing at a3, right: b3 is adjacent B. No opponent disc between. So no.
But wait, right line needs W or B? Need to trap opponent (White) between a3 and a B. So right from a3: b3 is B (own color?). When placing Black at a3, we need a line of White ending in Black. So right: b3 is B. That's own color immediately. No.
Down: a4 is B. Own color immediately. No.
Down-right: b4 is B. Own color. No.
Actually, from a3, are there any white lines ending in black?
Let's check each direction:
- Up: a2 is W. a1 is W. Then off board. No black at end. No.
- Up-right: b2 is W. c1 is W. d0 off board. No.
- Right: b3 is B. No white in between. No.
- Down-right: b4 is B. No.
- Down: a4 is B. No.
- Down-left: off board.
- Left: off board.
- Up-left: off board.
Wait, could a3 trap something like a6? No. So a3 is NOT legal for Black after a1? But the empty squares include a3 and b6 etc. The puzzle said legal moves are g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8 at the start. After White moves, new legal moves appear. But we need to see if Black has moves after a1.

Let's check b6 for Black after White a1.
b6: up: b5 B. No. Down: b7 . empty. Left: a6 W. Then? a7 . empty? Wait a7 is empty. So left from b6: a6 W. No black beyond. No.
Right: c6 B. Own color. No.
Up-right: c5 W. d4 W? d4 was flipped to W by a1. e3 W? f2 B. So b6 up-right: c5(W), d4(W), e3(W), f2(B). So c5, d4, e3 are White between b6 and f2. Yes! So b6 flips c5, d4, e3.
Also up-left: a5 B. No white between. No.
Down-right: c7 W. d8 W. e7? Wait d8 is W. c7 W. d8 W. e9 off. Is there a black beyond? e8 is B. But from b6 down-right: c7(W), d8(W), e9(off). Not a line to e8. Let's trace: b6 -> c7 -> d8 -> e9. Off board after d8. So no. Actually is there a black at the end? No.
Down: b7 empty. No.
So b6 is legal for Black (up-right line).
Any other?

a7 for Black:
Check all directions.
Up: a6 W. Up-right: b6 . empty. Right: b7 . empty. Down: a8 . empty. Down-right: b8 . empty. Left/up-left etc off board. Up: a6 W, then a5 B. So a7 up: a6(W), a5(B). Flips a6. Yes! So a7 flips a6.
Are there any other lines? Up-right: b6 empty. Right: b7 empty. So a7 is legal (flips a6).

b7 for Black:
Up: b6 . empty. Up-left: a6 W. Then a5 B. So b7 up-left: a6(W), a5(B). Flips a6.
Right: c7 W. d7 W. e7 W. f7 W. g7 W. h7 B. So right flips c7,d7,e7,f7,g7. That's 5 discs.
Down-right: c8 . empty. Down: b8 . empty. Down-left: a8 . empty. Left: a7 . empty. Up-right: c6 B. No white between. So b7 flips a6 and c7-g7. That's huge. So b7 is legal and very strong.

a8 for Black:
Up: a7 . empty. Right: b8 . empty. Up-right: b7 . empty. Down off board. So probably not legal.

b8 for Black:
Up: b7 . empty. Right: c8 . empty. Up-right: c7 W. d7 W. e7 W. f7 W. g7 W. h7 B. So b8 up-right: c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 to h7 B. Flips 5 discs.
Down-right off board. Left: a8 empty. Up-left: a7 empty. So b8 is legal, flipping c7-g7.
